newsitem.title: USA: American Electric Power sees $111 mln UK tax. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: American Electric Power sees $111 mln UK tax. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: American Electric Power said Wednesday it expects its assessment under a proposed UK utility windfall tax will be $111 million.
(Corrects figure in headline and text from $11 million).

In April AEP purchased a 50 percent interest in Yorkshire Electricity Group, a regional electric company in the UK. AEP said its share of Yorkshire's earnings increased nonoperating income by $4.1 million in the second quarter.
The company today reported second quarter earnings excluding the effect of the UK's proposed one-time windfall profits tax on privatized U.K. utilities.

"We are currently assessing the net earnings effect of the proposed tax, which is expected to be recorded when the proposed tax is enacted in the third quarter of 1997," said Chief Executive E. Linn Draper.
"AEP's share of the proposed tax is estimated to be about $111 million," the company said in a statement.

American Electric Power said net income for the second quarter rose to $121.1 million, or $0.64 a share, from $112.7 million, or $0.60 a share, a year earlier. Operating revenues decreased to $1.38 billion from $1.40 billion.
